\chapter{Learning Theory — Sub Gaussian}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.JohnsonLindenstrauss.SubGaussian
\section{Overview}

This module is the sub-Gaussian abstraction layer for the Johnson--Lindenstrauss
lemma.  Its main result, \texttt{subgaussian\_centered\_sq\_bernstein}
(Vershynin, Proposition~2.7.1(e), the MGF form of the sub-Gaussian/sub-exponential
link of Lemma~2.7.6; the scalar diagonal case of the Hanson--Wright circle of results,
Theorem~6.2.1), shows that if $Z$ is
strictly sub-Gaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2$ and $\E[Z^2] = \sigma^2$, then
the centered square $Z^2 - \sigma^2$ satisfies the Bernstein MGF condition with
parameters $(2\sigma^4, 1/(4\sigma^2))$.  The supporting lemmas provide a Gaussian
decoupling identity (the trick used in the proof of Vershynin's Lemma~6.2.2), an elementary quadratic bound on $e^{-x}$, an exponential-moment
bound for $Z^2$, a fourth-moment bound, and the two one-sided centered MGF bounds.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian decoupling identity]
\lean{exp_mul_sq_eq_integral_gaussian}
\label{exp_mul_sq_eq_integral_gaussian}
\leanok
For every real $t \ge 0$ and every real $z$,
\[
  e^{t z^2} \;=\; \int e^{\sqrt{2t}\, z\, g}\, \mathrm{d}N(0,1)(g),
\]
i.e.\ $e^{tz^2}$ equals the moment generating function of a standard Gaussian
evaluated at $s = \sqrt{2t}\, z$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Quadratic upper bound on $e^{-x}$]
\lean{exp_neg_le_one_sub_add_sq_div_two}
\label{exp_neg_le_one_sub_add_sq_div_two}
\leanok
For every real $x \ge 0$,
\[
  e^{-x} \;\le\; 1 - x + \frac{x^2}{2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exponential moment of $Z^2$ for a sub-Gaussian $Z$]
\lean{integral_exp_mul_sq_le_of_subgaussian}
\label{integral_exp_mul_sq_le_of_subgaussian}
\leanok
\uses{exp_mul_sq_eq_integral_gaussian, integrable_exp_mul_sq_gaussianReal_zero, integral_exp_mul_sq_gaussianReal_zero}
Let $Z$ be a measurable real random variable on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$
which is strictly sub-Gaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2$: for every real $s$,
$e^{sZ}$ is $\mu$-integrable and $\E_\mu[e^{sZ}] \le e^{\sigma^2 s^2/2}$.  Then for every
$t \ge 0$ with $2\sigma^2 t < 1$, the function $e^{tZ^2}$ is $\mu$-integrable and
\[
  \E_\mu\!\left[e^{t Z^2}\right] \;\le\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - 2\sigma^2 t}},
\]
the same bound that holds for $Z \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fourth-moment bound for a sub-Gaussian $Z$]
\lean{integral_pow_four_le_of_subgaussian}
\label{integral_pow_four_le_of_subgaussian}
\leanok
\uses{integral_exp_mul_sq_le_of_subgaussian}
Let $Z$ be a measurable real random variable on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$
which is strictly sub-Gaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2 > 0$ (for every real $s$,
$e^{sZ}$ is integrable and $\E_\mu[e^{sZ}] \le e^{\sigma^2 s^2/2}$), and suppose
$\E_\mu[Z^2] = \sigma^2$.  Then $Z^4$ is $\mu$-integrable and
\[
  \E_\mu\!\left[Z^4\right] \;\le\; 4\sigma^4 .
\]
(For a Gaussian the exact value is $3\sigma^4$.)
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Centered-square MGF bound, nonpositive $t$]
\lean{mgf_centered_sq_le_of_nonpos}
\label{mgf_centered_sq_le_of_nonpos}
\leanok
\uses{exp_neg_le_one_sub_add_sq_div_two, integral_pow_four_le_of_subgaussian}
Let $Z$ be a measurable real random variable on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$
which is strictly sub-Gaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2 > 0$ (for every real $s$,
$e^{sZ}$ is integrable and $\E_\mu[e^{sZ}] \le e^{\sigma^2 s^2/2}$), with
$\E_\mu[Z^2] = \sigma^2$.  Then for every $t$ with $-1/(4\sigma^2) \le t \le 0$, the
function $e^{t(Z^2 - \sigma^2)}$ is $\mu$-integrable and
\[
  \E_\mu\!\left[e^{t(Z^2 - \sigma^2)}\right] \;\le\; e^{2\sigma^4 t^2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Centered-square MGF bound, nonnegative $t$]
\lean{mgf_centered_sq_le_of_nonneg}
\label{mgf_centered_sq_le_of_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{integral_exp_mul_sq_le_of_subgaussian, neg_log_one_sub_two_mul_le_two_sq}
Let $Z$ be a measurable real random variable on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$
which is strictly sub-Gaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2 > 0$ (for every real $s$,
$e^{sZ}$ is integrable and $\E_\mu[e^{sZ}] \le e^{\sigma^2 s^2/2}$).  Then for every
$t$ with $0 \le t \le 1/(4\sigma^2)$, the function $e^{t(Z^2 - \sigma^2)}$ is
$\mu$-integrable and
\[
  \E_\mu\!\left[e^{t(Z^2 - \sigma^2)}\right] \;\le\; e^{2\sigma^4 t^2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Sub-Gaussian implies sub-exponential centered square]
\lean{subgaussian_centered_sq_bernstein}
\label{subgaussian_centered_sq_bernstein}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF, mgf_centered_sq_le_of_nonneg, mgf_centered_sq_le_of_nonpos}
Let $Z$ be a measurable real random variable on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$
which is strictly sub-Gaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2 > 0$, i.e.\ for every real
$t$ the function $e^{tZ}$ is $\mu$-integrable and $\E_\mu[e^{tZ}] \le e^{\sigma^2 t^2/2}$,
and whose second moment is exactly $\E_\mu[Z^2] = \sigma^2$.  Then the centered square
$Z^2 - \sigma^2$ satisfies the Bernstein MGF condition
\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF} with parameters $(2\sigma^4,\, 1/(4\sigma^2))$:
for every $t$ with $\abs{t} \le 1/(4\sigma^2)$, $e^{t(Z^2 - \sigma^2)}$ is
$\mu$-integrable and $\E_\mu[e^{t(Z^2 - \sigma^2)}] \le e^{2\sigma^4 t^2}$.  This is the
sub-exponential MGF bound of Vershynin, Proposition~2.7.1(e), for the square of a
sub-Gaussian variable (the sub-Gaussian/sub-exponential link of Lemma~2.7.6), i.e.\ the
scalar case of the Hanson--Wright circle of results (Theorem~6.2.1), with the sharp
Gaussian-case constants; the Gaussian decoupling identity it rests on is the one from
Vershynin's Lemma~6.2.2.
\end{theorem}
